title: fix(process): tree-kill the nohup'd worker in sandbox background kills
claim: Killing a sandbox-backed (docker/ssh/modal/...) background process must terminate the nohup'd user command, not only the wrapper subshell whose PID is recorded.

evidence.red: NOT_TESTED (owned upstream). Need confirmed by source: main tools/process_registry.py spawn_via_env L1400-1404 `( nohup bash -lc CMD > log 2>&1; rc=$?; ... ) & echo $! > pid` records the wrapper PID, and _signal_kill sandbox branch runs `kill {session.pid}` only.

upstream_overlap: #125004 (OPEN, MERGEABLE, Adolanium, 2026-09-27) 'fix(process): kill the whole sandbox background tree, not just the wrapper', Fixes #125003 (OPEN). Uses `set -m` + `kill -TERM -- -<pgid>` + `trap : TERM` so the exit file still records 143, with a real-bash TestSandboxKillTree.
#129674 / #128735 (OPEN, Froraut) sandbox background jobs cwd/exit/log, adjacent.
notes: #125004 is smaller (+10/-4 prod) and keeps exit-code capture; ours adds a .worker_pid artifact plus a local.py cleanup regex change. Not worth competing. Possible review support on #125004: verify group kill when the sandbox shell lacks job control, and SIGKILL escalation parity with the host path (ours had TERM->KILL escalation). Kanban baggage ignored.
